source_paper.title: Multiscale Spatial Transcriptomic Atlas of Human Basal Ganglia Cell-Type and Cellular Community Organization
source_paper.pages_analyzed: 1-25 (title, highlights, abstract, intro, results, discussion through 'Limitations'); remainder of 80-page PDF is Methods/figures/references/supplement

EntityExtractor.masking_rationale: First pass surfaced abundant overlapping cell-type/gene tokens (e.g. STR TAC3-PLPP4 contains gene tokens TAC3 and PLPP4). A second masked-text pass was run to catch standalone gene mentions and indirect references that the cell-type extraction round had absorbed. A third round was not warranted: the masked-text re-scan yielded only incremental gene/molecule entities and no new entity classes.

source_sentences: The human basal ganglia is a critical brain structure involved in motor control, learning and emotion.
We generated a multi-region, subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomic atlas of the human basal ganglia by integrating MERFISH+ and Stereo-seq across four neurotypical donors.

indirect_references.source_sentence: It is comprised of distinct anatomical nuclei / subdivisions including the striatum, the globus pallidus, and the nucleus accumbens.

source_sentences: We obtained four postmortem human brain fresh frozen slabs across anterior-to-posterior segments of the basal ganglia encompassing the caudate nucleus, putamen, nucleus accumbens (NAc), globus pallidus, and internal capsule.
the putamen exhibits strong enrichment of ZNF385B and ROBO2
The nucleus accumbens, located at the ventral extension of the striatum, contains both D1 and D2 MSNs and is further divided into core and shell subregions.
